result:
There's no repo content here to inspect (empty working directory), so I can't verify the diff myself — I'll go on what you've described. Here's my read:

**The uniqueness-test risk is the real one, and "green" doesn't clear it.** A validation library that improves Unicode handling very plausibly changed *normalization* behavior — e.g., whether it applies Unicode NFC/NFD normalization, case-folds differently, or now accepts characters that decompose to the same visual/logical name (confusables, combining diacritics, full-width vs half-width forms, Turkish dotless-I, etc.). That's exactly the kind of change a "minor perf gains + better Unicode" changelog line hides, and it's exactly the kind of change existing uniqueness tests won't catch unless they were written with adversarial Unicode cases in mind. If your existing tests only assert ASCII names and maybe a couple of accented examples, "still green" tells you the old behavior didn't regress for those inputs — it tells you nothing about whether two visually-different (or visually-identical) strings now collide or diverge differently than before.

Concretely, ask: did test coverage include things like `"Bengt"` vs `"Bengt"` with a combining vs precomposed é, or Turkish `İ`/`I`/`ı`/`i` case folding, before *and* after the bump? If not, green suite isn't evidence either way.

**What I'd actually want before merging today:**
1. Read the 3.3.0 diff/changelog on the library itself (not just your package.json diff) — specifically whether it touched normalization, case-folding, or trimming logic, not just character-class allowlists.
2. Add a handful of adversarial uniqueness tests: same name in different Unicode normalization forms, mixed scripts, Turkish/Vietnamese diacritic edge cases — confirm behavior is either unchanged or changed in the direction you want.
3. Since usernames are user-visible identity and go through a uniqueness check, a behavior change here is a data-integrity concern, not just a validation-regex concern — worth 30-60 minutes even under deadline pressure.

DB-parameterization being fine is true but irrelevant to this risk — the risk is two different-looking usernames colliding (or two same-looking ones not), not injection.

If you can point me at the actual package.json/lockfile diff or the validation call site in this repo, I can check more concretely — right now this working directory appears empty.
